title: Backplane skipcount anomaly - field diary and runbook sketch
content:
Summary:

This is an on-call field diary and initial runbook sketch for a recurring "skipcount" anomaly we observed across a multi-node rack (3 nodes, 6 GPUs each) on 2027-11-02 -> 2027-11-04. Symptoms are short-lived drops in PCIe/NVLink-like backplane packet sequencing (we see sequence numbers jump / skipcount) accompanied by short bursts of correctable ECC and occasional driver hangs that, in one instance, escalated to a kernel panic when coupled with a suspicious firmware watchdog timer expiry.

Why this doc exists:
- Collect chronological evidence from night shift triage.
- Capture minimal repro steps and runbook candidates (fast mitigation for oncall).
- Surface telemetry and alert tuning proposals so noisy but low-impact events don't drown real outages.

High-level hypothesis (working):
- A transient PHY-level negotiation hiccup in the backplane link causes a small number of lanes to re-establish without preserving ordering, resulting in a small window where sequence counters appear to "skip". That triggers downstream error-handling code in the driver which increments correctable ECC counters due to misaligned packets, and in some cases trips a firmware recovery path that interacts poorly with the kernel driver leading to a stack lock-up.

Observed signals (raw):
- Link-layer counters: link_seq_mismatch +14 events between 03:18-03:24 UTC on node-rack3-nd07.
- ECC correctable: +260 on GPU0 over 6 minutes, correlated to CPU IRQ spikes.
- dmesg excerpt (trimmed):
  [Nov 2 03:19:12] gpu0: nvbp: seq_mismatch: expected 0x1f4 got 0x234 (skipcount 0x40)
  [Nov 2 03:19:13] kernel: gpu-driver: GPU0 hung in user stream, dumping stacks
  [Nov 2 03:19:14] gpu-fw: watchdog: scheduling reset (reason: unacked-evt)
- Journalctl: driver reinit logstorm then an oops on node-rack3-nd07 at 03:19:15 (stack trace attached in linked artifact).

Triage timeline (night-shift notes):
- 03:17 UTC: Alert: surge of correctable ECC on rack3. Pager to eng-sre.
- 03:18 UTC: Oncall (Ava) jumped to ssh into node-rack3-nd07, observed link_seq_mismatch metrics via /proc/backplane_stats.
- 03:20 UTC: Attempted soft-reset of GPU0 driver (rmmod/modprobe). Driver did not rebind cleanly; kernel reported blocked workqueue.
- 03:24 UTC: Performed host-level soft reboot of node; node came back clean but two GPUs showed elevated ECC credits in telemetry.
- 03:55 UTC: Similar low-volume events on node-rack3-nd05; pattern matched sequence count jumps but no panic.

Repro attempts (lab):
- Replayed high-throughput microbench (continuous small messages across backplane) on a replica rack in lab (same firmware revision) for 12 hours: reproduced faint sequence mismatches at ~0.1/hr.
- Injected PHY-reset via debug tool during sustained load: reproducible sequence skip when reset aligned with a large in-flight KV cache swap.
- Increased link training retry thresholds in firmware: reduced observed skipcount events by ~70% in controlled test (small sample).

Quick mitigations for oncall (P0->hotfix path):
- If sequence-mismatch > threshold (configurable, e.g., 50 in 10 minutes) and driver shows hung workqueue -> escalate to node reboot. Owner: oncall.
- If single-node isolated burst of ECC < threshold and no hangs: throttle workload to node out via autoscaler for 10 mins and set node drain reason "backplane-skip-priority". Owner: SRE shift.
- Temp firmware rollback to previous release is an option only if we see crash rate increase and can schedule maintenance window. Owner: infra-firmware.

Runbook sketch (draft steps for first responder):
1) Confirm: query /proc/backplane_stats, dmesg | grep seq_mismatch, and GPU ECC counters via metrics (prometheus label: node, gpu_id).
2) If seq_mismatch count trending up rapidly AND driver hangs present: collect full vmcore (if kdump enabled) and schedule immediate node reboot; create incident channel and ping infra-firmware and oncall kernel engineer.
3) If only ECC correctables increasing and no driver hangs: mark node for short drain (10-30 mins), set qps limit on serving route, and watch for reversion to baseline.
4) If reproduces on >1 node in same rack within 2 hours: escalate to rack-level maintenance (rack taken to maintenance mode).
5) Gather logs: /var/log/dmesg, /proc/backplane_stats snapshot, firmware telemetry (fetch via fw-tool get-telemetry --range=10m), and link training trace. Attach to Jira ticket.

Alert & dashboard tuning proposals (reduce noise):
- Lower-level: Create an "early-warning" metric that tracks short-lived sequence-mismatch bursts without firing a pager (SEV3). Pager only on condition: seq_mismatch_rate >= 100 AND driver_hang=true OR kernel_panic=true.
- Dashboard: per-rack heatmap for sequence_mismatch normalized by link-util to separate noisy high-util nodes from pathological nodes.
- Alert suppression: ignore single gpu spikes when corrected ECC/ minute < 5 and no hangs for 30 minutes.

Telemetry / instrumentation gaps noticed:
- Link-layer traces are coarse (1s bins) — we need sub-100ms sampling around training windows.
- No correlation id across firmware telemetry and kernel driver logs; add a short-lived correlation token emitted by fw on every training event.
- Prometheus scrape rate for per-gpu link counters is 15s; increase to 5s for selected canaries and add a rolling buffer for postmortem.

Longer-term engineering suggestions (backlog items):
- Add ordered-packet guard in driver: on small sequence discontinuities allow a brief re-sequencing window before escalating to recovery path. This reduces overactive recovery for recoverable skipcounts. Owner: driver-team.
- Firmware: add negotiated-lane-mapping epoch that is monotonically increasing and emitted on link retrain; driver verifies epoch before declaring packets stale. Owner: infra-firmware.
- Investigate interaction between KV cache eviction at scale and PHY retrain timing — hypothesis: large KV swaps push a write-window that coincides with micro-reset leading to reorder. Owner: serving-runtime + applied-ml.

Evidence inventory (to attach to Jira-CORE-5921):
- Lab repro logs: git://infra/repro-harness/skipcount-repro/2027-11-03.tar.gz
- Node journal snippets (sensitive) uploaded to secure doc store: link in Jira ticket.
- Stack trace from kernel panic (x86): included in attachments.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some nodes tolerate the same skipcount bursts with no hangs? Hardware variance, subtle firmware timing, or different background CPU load?
- Is there correlation with specific job types (large KV-cache ops) or certain models/sequence lengths? We have an early signal but need workload-tagged traces.

Next steps (short horizon):
- 24h: implement alert-change to SEV3 for transient bursts; add 5s scrape for two rack canaries. Owner: observability.
- 72h: lab reproducibility plan complete and experiment to validate firmware rollback vs link-training tweak. Owner: infra-firmware + SRE.
- 2w: draft driver patch for tolerant re-sequencing window and test harness. Owner: driver-team.

Notes to self / oncall tips:
- When collecting logs, run: sudo cat /proc/backplane_stats > /tmp/bp-$(date +%s).txt and fw-tool get-telemetry --range=5m --format=json > /tmp/fw-telemetry.json. These two files are the fastest to attach to a ticket.
- If forced to do node reboot, ensure you deallocate active dedicated sessions via console prior to power-cycle to avoid customer-visible RPC timeouts.

Appendix: quick checklist for field runbook (one-liner form)
- Look at sequence-mismatch metric, ECC delta, dmesg for gpu-driver oops.
- If driver hung: dump+reboot.
- If correctables only: throttle and drain (10-30m).
- If multi-node same rack: rack maintenance.

This remains a working document. Please add notes or paste pastebin links to the Jira ticket. If you touch firmware or driver config in prod, update the "prod-config-change-log" spreadsheet and ping oncall-announce.

-- Ava
